messages.author: 5fa2a363d4ddd1d1
messages.subject: NIMBLE version 0.6-6 released
parts:
Dear nimble-users and nimble-announce:

We’ve just released the newest version of NIMBLE on CRAN and on our
website. Version 0.6-6 has some important new features, and more are
on the way in the next few months.

New features include:

- dynamic indexes are now allowed in BUGS code — indexes of a variable
no longer need to be constants but can be other nodes or functions of
other nodes; for this release this is a beta feature that needs to be
enabled with nimbleOptions(allowDynamicIndexing = TRUE) and please let
us know of any issues you notice;
- the intrinsic Gaussian CAR (conditional autoregressive) model can
now be used in BUGS code as dcar_normal, which behaves similarly to
BUGS’ car.normal distribution;
- optim is now part of the NIMBLE language and can be used in nimbleFunctions;
- it is possible to call out to external compiled code or back to R
functions from a nimbleFunction using nimbleExternalCall() and
nimbleRcall() (this is an experimental feature so again feedback is
particularly welcome);
- the WAIC model selection criterion can be calculated using the
calculateWAIC() method for MCMC objects;
- the bootstrap and auxiliary particle filters can now return their ESS values;
- and a variety of bug fixes.

Please see the NEWS file in the installed package for more details.

Finally, we’re deep in the midst of development work to enable
automatic differentiation, Tensorflow as an alternative back-end
computational engine, additional spatial models, and Bayesian
nonparametrics.

- Chris Paciorek for the NIMBLE Development Team

messages.author: 5fa2a363d4ddd1d1
messages.subject: Re: NIMBLE version 0.6-6 released
parts:
Ideally you would install with administrative access (or have your
administrator do it) in the usual location on your Windows computer.
That being said, if you install it somewhere else and pay attention to
the various "pages" as you go through the installation procedure, I
suspect the main thing is to make sure that wherever you install it is
added to your PATH so that R knows where to find the compiler tools.
